summary: Milestone 2026.04.99's supplied operational closeout slice was short and orchestration-bound: 10 minutes total wall time, 2 completed conductor items, and a 5 minute average per item. The only material slow path was the 10 minute arXiv Bundle v10 slot, which was correctly gated on exp1269 paper critical fixes and ended with a compiled bundle plus upload pending. Current GPU telemetry showed both RTX 3090s idle at 4 MB and 0% utilization with no GPU processes, so no gpu_monitor.py-class zombie waste was present. The pre-flight suite was not the visible bottleneck; serial gate/doc coupling and unused DualGPU capacity were the main recoverable losses.

slowest_experiments.title: arXiv Bundle v10 - Gated on Exp 1269 Critical Fixes
slowest_experiments.why_long: This was the only material critical-path item in the supplied timing slice. It waited on exp1269, then compiled docs/arxiv-paper/main.tex with tectonic and wrote results/carnot-arxiv-v10-20260504.tar.gz. The runtime was legitimate gate plus TeX bundle work, not GPU compute.

slowest_experiments.title: In-process docs for arXiv Bundle v10 - Gated on Exp 1269 Critical Fixes
slowest_experiments.why_long: No material wall-clock cost was visible in the provided timing. The docs path was tied to the arXiv bundle but did not independently bottleneck this slice.

bottlenecks_identified: The operational closeout was dominated by one serial publication gate: exp1270 could only run after exp1269 critical paper fixes were terminal.

GPU utilization was inefficient for the milestone as a whole. Current gpu_monitor.py telemetry showed both RTX 3090s idle at 4 MB and 0% utilization, so the available DualGPU lane was unused during closeout.
No material zombie GPU processes were present. gpu_monitor.py reported an empty process list and no warnings; the 4 MB per GPU looked like negligible driver/context residue.

Pre-flight was not the bottleneck in this slice. Existing changelog evidence records focused 81-test pre-flight checks on the order of seconds, while the supplied wall time was consumed by gate and bundle sequencing.

The arXiv/docs critical path was too serial. Bundle compilation, changelog reconciliation, and roadmap confirmation were handled as closeout work instead of being prepared asynchronously once exp1269 completed.
Doc reconciliation was cheap in this 10 minute slice, but repeated .99 operational-retro changelog entries show the broader process lacks idempotent update semantics.

Structured timing is still too thin: the supplied slowest list had only coarse minute buckets, so root-cause attribution depends on artifact/changelog inference rather than first-class conductor fields.
improvements_suggested: Launch independent CPU/data tasks and any GPU-capable validation lane while publication packaging waits on paper gates.
Promote gpu_monitor.py output into scheduler decisions: if both GPUs are idle and queued work can use live models, start a DualGPURunner lane or write an explicit blocked reason.
Cache TeX dependencies and add a narrow arXiv bundle preflight target so exp1270 can fail fast on missing tools before it enters the critical path.
Record per-experiment timing fields in result artifacts: queued_at, started_at, gated_wait_s, preflight_s, execution_s, docs_reconcile_s, and finished_at.
Make operational retro/changelog updates idempotent for a milestone so repeated recovery passes update one bullet or append a clearly versioned refresh line instead of accumulating near-duplicates.
Emit structured blocked artifacts for gated tasks immediately; do not spend agent time rediscovering that a prerequisite is unavailable.
Batch docs reconciliation after terminal artifacts are written, and keep roadmap row insertion duplicate-aware.
estimated_time_savings_rationale: A 30% saving is realistic for the next similar closeout: roughly 10-15% from overlapping independent CPU/GPU work with publication gating, 5-8% from cached TeX/pre-flight state, 5% from structured gate-block artifacts, and 5% from idempotent batched docs reconciliation. On a 10 minute slice that is only a few minutes, but the same fixes matter more when the milestone has many gated tasks.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Run GPU-capable experiments in a dedicated DualGPURunner lane whenever gpu_monitor.py reports both cards idle.
Add first-class conductor timing fields separating gate wait, pre-flight, execution, and docs reconciliation.
Make docs and roadmap reconciliation idempotent and batch it after terminal artifacts exist.

gpu_utilization.assessment: Inefficient from a resource-scheduling perspective. The closeout was not GPU-bound, but the idle DualGPU capacity should have been used for independent model-bearing work if any remained queued.

zombie_process_assessment.basis: scripts/gpu_monitor.py --json at 2026-05-04T19:20:40.830451+00:00 reported no GPU processes and no warnings.
zombie_process_assessment.note: The 4 MB allocations on each RTX 3090 are negligible and do not meet the monitor's zombie definition.

preflight_assessment: Not a bottleneck for this closeout slice. The visible prior .99 operational notes cite focused 81-test checks under roughly 8 seconds; the supplied 10 minute wall time is explained by serial gate and bundle work instead.
doc_reconciliation_assessment: The in-process docs item was listed as 0 minutes, so it did not materially slow this slice. The broader doc process should still be tightened because ops/changelog.md already contains multiple .99 operational-retro refresh entries for the same artifact.
parallelization_assessment: exp1270 itself could not be parallelized before exp1269 completed, but non-publication tasks in the 1268-1281 range could have run in parallel lanes. The next milestone should keep one CPU/docs lane and one GPU/model lane active rather than waiting for publication packaging to clear.

question_answers.which_experiments_took_longest_and_why: exp1270 took 10 minutes and was the only material slow item. It was slow because it sat on the paper/arXiv critical path after exp1269 and performed actual TeX bundle compilation plus packaging. The docs item registered 0 minutes.
question_answers.was_gpu_utilization_efficient: No. Both RTX 3090s were idle at 4 MB and 0% utilization. The closeout work was CPU/docs-bound, but the scheduler still left available GPU capacity unused.
question_answers.were_there_zombie_processes: No. gpu_monitor.py reported no GPU processes and no warnings, so there were no material zombie processes wasting VRAM.
question_answers.could_any_experiments_have_been_parallel: Yes. exp1270 was gate-dependent, but other non-publication tasks in the .99 range could have overlapped with docs or GPU-capable validation lanes.
question_answers.was_the_pre_flight_test_suite_a_bottlene: No. Available .99 notes point to focused pre-flight checks in seconds, not minutes.
question_answers.were_doc_reconciliation_passes_efficient: Partly. The in-process docs slot was effectively free in this slice, but repeated .99 changelog refreshes show reconciliation should be idempotent and batched.
question_answers.what_tooling_would_speed_up_the_next_mil: GPU-aware scheduling from gpu_monitor.py, DualGPURunner-by-default for queued model work, cached TeX/pre-flight targets, structured per-experiment timing, immediate blocked artifacts for unmet gates, and idempotent docs reconciliation.

meta_reflection: The main operational lesson is that .99 was no longer losing hours to failed compute; it was losing small but repeatable minutes to serial closeout mechanics. That is a better failure mode, but it still compounds. The next milestone should make the conductor prove that idle GPUs are either used or explicitly blocked, and should make docs updates deterministic rather than a repeated agent chore.
